schedule: Refreshed three times a day (5:17 AM, 12:17 PM and 6:17 PM ET) by a scheduled research run.
live_note: Day seven, Tuesday morning: America's cyber agency has formally listed the flaws as exploited. CISA added CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct 26 (version 2026.10.26, released 22:24 UTC; this run opened the feed directly), with a federal deadline of Oct 29; the third flaw, CVE-2026-115560, is not listed and still has no fix. CISA named no victim and described no attack, and no organization has confirmed a breach by name (ZDNet Korea, Oct 27); Wiz says it has seen no end-to-end success in its own data and that scanner IPs which succeeded against Adel Karimi's decoy servers 'likely contributed' to the listing. So the running story stays PROVEN, not HIT. New numbers: TU Delft's sensors count 57,097 exploitation requests from 626 IPs in 71 countries since Oct 21 (attempts, not successes); Japan has paused 1,090 sites and services, about 40% not yet back (Assured, via ANN/ABEMA); Wiz sees vulnerable exposed machines down about 67%; Censys still counts 32.51M PHP services on an affected version (via The Hacker News). The index's forecast that CISA would list the flaws by Oct 31 resolved yes; it was called a toss-up (50%), so it does not count toward the record either way.
live_since_label: hours since the PHP fix shipped (Oct 21, about 14:00 UTC)

No change to PHP2Shell. serial.name: The flaw under most websites
serial.standing: America's cyber agency now lists two of the flaws as used in real attacks. No real victim has been named. A third flaw is still unfixed.
serial.recheck: still no organization confirmed breached by name, still no fix for the third flaw

next_test.text: Will a real organization confirm it was broken into through the flaw under most websites?

serial.strip: US cyber agency confirms attacks. No named victim yet.

lead.tag: America's cyber agency: hackers are using the flaw under most websites
lead.standfirst: America's cyber agency (CISA) added two of the PHP flaws to its list of flaws known to be used in real attacks on Oct 26, and gave federal agencies until Oct 29 to fix them. It named no victim, and no organization has confirmed a breach, so this stays Proven, not Hit.

you.touch: If you run a website, this is the moment to check it: the US government now says these flaws are being used in real attacks, and most websites run on PHP. If you don't run one, there's nothing to do, though some services you use may pause while they fix it.
today: Ask your web host or developer: is our site on a PHP version fixed on or after Oct 21?

site.touch: Your site is exposed if it runs PHP on a version from before Oct 21; the US government now lists two of the flaws as used in real attacks. A third flaw has no fix yet; PHP's advice is a temporary workaround.
today: Check your PHP version with your host today, and update or take the site offline until you can.
